pompe.match_text:
Painting on wood panel of sacrificial procession from Pitsa (cave of the Charites) - Athen NAM 16464 - object type: tempera painting on wood panel (plaque)
- description: sacrificial procession of a family, with name inscriptions in the corinthian alphabet: bearded man holding twigs, woman (EUTHYDIKA) holding twigs, woman (EUQOLIS), youth playing auloi, boy playing lyra, boy leading a lamb to sacrifice, woman ((ETH)ELONGCHA) carrying a tablet with offerings on her head, holding oinochoe, altar;
around the upper and right rim: dedication-inscription to the Charites (Graces), by ... (Name of the dedicator or of the painter illegible) from Corinth: ... QORINTHIOS
- period / date: ripe archaic, ca. 540-530 BC
- findspot: Pitsa (near Sikyon), cult cave of the Charites, found together with 3 more fragments of painted dedicative wood panels
- museum / inventory number: Athens, National Archaeological Museum 16464

- Please note: The above museum permits photography of its exhibits for private, educational, scientific, non-commercial purposes. If you intend to use the photo for any commercial aime, please contact the museum and ask for permission. Pitsa Panel, NAMA 16464|Self-published work

- period / date: high archaic, ca. (560-)550 BC
